chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Jaroud ibn al-Munthir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the soul of one of you reaches this (point)', and he gestured with his hand to his throat, his eyes would be delighted (i.e., he would die with a good ending).

key_terms.قَرَّتْ عَيْنُهُ: His eye was cooled (metaphor for peace/relief)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the soul reaching the throat in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the throat as the exit point of the soul (ruh), linking the physical sensation of the soul's departure to the spiritual state of 'cooling of the eye,' a key concept in Shia eschatology denoting relief from the trials of death. This specific anatomical marker is often discussed by scholars in conjunction with the concept of *Barzakh* (the intermediate realm), emphasizing that the quality of one's death is determined by the soul's ease or distress during this transition. The hadith thus serves as a practical indicator for believers to assess their spiritual state and prepare for the moment of *husn al-khatimah*.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Safwan, from Jaroud Bin Al Munzar who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the soul of one of you reaches this (point)’, and he<sup>asws</sup> gestured with his<sup>asws</sup> hand to his<sup>asws</sup> throat, his eyes would be delighted’.
en.sarwar: 14. It is narrated from him (narrator of the above Hadith) from Safwan from Jarud ibn al-Mundhir who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘When the soul of one of you reaches here’ - pointing to his throat - ‘his eyes become delightful.’”
